content.text:
I fixed it: the broken-anchor check now matches a link like `/docs/php/tooling#phpunit` to the page whether or not the link has a trailing slash. The existing broken-links tests pass (34/34). I didn't add a new test for this exact case, and I didn't run the reporter's repo.

**Cause:** the plain broken-link check already allowed for trailing slashes, but the anchor check didn't. It looked up the target page by its exact pathname. That page was recorded during the build as `/docs/php/tooling/`, so the lookup for `/docs/php/tooling` found nothing. Any anchor on it was then reported as broken, even though the page itself loads fine.

**Fix:** in `packages/docusaurus/src/server/brokenLinks.ts`, I added a small helper, `getPageCollectedLinks`. It tries the pathname as given, its decoded form, and the with- and without-slash version of each, then uses the first page it finds. `isAnchorBrokenLink` now uses this helper instead of the exact lookup.

The anchor check now accepts either form for any page, even where a route is set to be strict about trailing slashes. That matches what the reporter saw in the browser.

The TypeScript warning at line 231 of the same file (`new Error(..., { cause })`) is about code I didn't change.
